This Profile Was the MVP & A Lot Could Be Improved

Also the previous profile design had a very low engagement. Even if the users who landed profile page, rarely submitted any details. So lets audit the previous design

1
Entry point buried in the side drawer

Profile was only accessible via the top hamburger menu → Profile. For most kirana owners using the app daily, the profile screen was effectively invisible.

2
No profile progress indicator — no motivation to complete

Users had no visibility of how complete their profile was, which fields were missing, or what they stood to gain by completing them. There was no feedback loop between action and reward.

3
40–50% of the screen was blank, wasted space

The profile had almost no content visible above the fold. Users landing here saw empty space and icons — no data, no sense of progress, no reason to engage further.

Project Objectives

  • Increase Profile views

    Improve Profile visibility in app, Preferably accessible from Home screen

  • More Shop photos & Shop Related data submission

    To understand their shop type, shop products

How might we motivate users to complete their profiles ?

In a way that feels natural, not forced ?

We Found Two Barriers — and Designed for Both

Barrier 1 · Discoverability

Invisible in the app

Profile lived behind a hamburger menu → side drawer. Daily users had no reason, and no easy path, to reach it.

☰ MenuSide DrawerProfilehidden
✕Zero visibility in daily purchase flow
Barrier 2 · Motivation

No reason to fill it in

No progress, no benefit, no hint of what was missing. For busy retailers, no visible payoff meant no effort.

?
✕No profile completion progress visible ✕No value communication for submitting data

Another big change

The Biggest Barrier Wasn’t Motivation — It Was Discoverability

Entrypoint to Profile

The side drawer got updated :

  • 1Can directly upload shop photos, more visibility to upload shop photos
  • 2Adding a profile progress bar

Scope kept tightNo other changes were made, to avoid unnecessary dev effort on new components.

12

Why this decision mattered?

  • 1Profile was buried inside Side Drawer menu, making it difficult for retailers to discover and revisit.
  • 2Moving Profile into the bottom navigation provided persistent visibility, making profile completion part of the core experience instead of a hidden task.

Scope kept tightNo other changes were made, to avoid unnecessary dev effort on new components.

New Bottom Nav bar got updated with Profile

Trade-off: Prioritizing Discoverability Over Familiarity

  1. Why Order Now was replaced

    Navigation analytics showed that Order Now had consistently low engagement, making it the lowest-value bottom navigation item and the best candidate for replacement.

  2. The cost: relearning a familiar nav

    We moved Profile into the bottom navigation even though users were already familiar with the previous navigation. It introduced short-term learnability efforts, but the long-term benefits outweighed them.

  3. The payoff: richer retailer profiles

    We prioritized profile discoverability over existing habits because richer retailer profiles directly supported KYC, customer segmentation, and future brand initiatives.

Decision stories

Where I had to convince

Three decisions where I argued my case, and where we ended up.

1

Adding a shareable business card

Evidence
The business card, shared on WhatsApp and promoting Badho
  1. Product lead Their argument

    Keep the profile to data collection. A generated card adds design, share and download work for V1.

  2. Me My counter

    The old profile gave retailers no reason to fill anything in. A business card is an instant payoff: they add their shop details, and Badho turns them into something they can share on WhatsApp or download to promote their own shop. And every time it’s shared, it also markets the Badho app.

  3. How we landed

    The card shipped in Badho’s brand colors for recall, as one fixed layout with Share and Download, so every share also promotes the app. Every state is designed, so the card is never empty.

In one line“Leads saw extra scope. I showed it was the payoff that makes retailers fill the profile in, and every share markets Badho, so we shipped it in Badho’s colors.”

2

Dropping profile badges, motivating through copy

Evidence
V1: badgesFinal: copy + progress
Copy on the screens
  • “Dukan ke photos ke bina aapki dukan ki pehchaan adhoori hai”
  • “More shop photos = More trust & better brand, seller matches!”
  • “Verify your profile to receive monthly payouts and brand schemes”
  • “Share your landmark and get product ideas based on the people around your shop”
  1. Dev / APM Their argument

    Badges need high tech effort for this release.

  2. Me My counter

    The goal was motivation, and badges were only one way to get it. Motivation comes from telling retailers what’s in it for them, in words they use, at the moment we ask them to act. So I wrote it into the screens, in simple Hinglish, with a reason for every ask.

  3. How we landed

    V2 and the final design have no badges. The copy, a progress bar and a Complete Profile button carry the motivation, with no extra build cost.

In one line“Badges needed high tech effort. I put the motivation into the copy instead: every prompt says what the retailer gets.”

3

Making KYC hard to miss

Evidence
V2: low emphasisFinal: nudge with states
  1. Stakeholders V2 feedback

    KYC has low emphasis. It needs to stand out.

  2. Me My counter

    KYC felt like an admin chore, so it got skipped. I tied it to the payoff already in the copy, monthly payouts and brand schemes, and made it a clear card with a Verify button and states for pending, in review and resubmit.

  3. How we landed

    The final design has a high-emphasis KYC nudge that handles multiple states.

In one line“V2 hid KYC, so I made it a benefit card with a button and states.”

My Learnings

💬Value communication is multiplier

Showing users why their profile data benefits them (better schemes, brand offers) was more effective than nudges alone. Users filled fields when they understood the payoff.

💰Profile completion unlocked a new B2B revenue stream

Rich store data enabled FMCG brands to identify and target specific retailer profiles — creating a new partnership and advertising channel for Badho.

🔎Profile can be a data gold mine

The more detailed user segmentation, the better we understand their preferences, their environment , goals. This data is a gold mine for detailed persona analysis.

Improvement areas

📈Event tracking for Business card share & downloads

Important to set up track business card share & downloads to measure adoption

🧩Better design for new section addition

When we added a new section in the profile later, it had quite lesser submission than other sections.

🧭Detailed user journey analysis

Which sections most users didn’t filled & why. We saw more submissions of photos than text inputs though.
